title: Task Orchestrator (DAG)
description: Build a DAG-based task orchestrator that resolves dependencies, parallelizes independent tasks, and handles failures.

steps.title: Create Task and DAG data structures
steps.description: Define a `Task` class with: `id` (string), `dependencies` (array of task IDs), `action` (function), `status` ('pending' | 'running' | 'completed' | 'failed'), `result`, and `duration`. Define a `DAG` class that holds a Map of tasks. Build a task graph with 5 tasks where task C depends on A, B; D depends on C; E depends on A. Print the full DAG structure showing each task and its dependencies.
hints: Use a Map<string, Task> for O(1) task lookup by id
Each task stores its dependencies as an array of other task IDs (not references)
Print the DAG as 'Task A -> []', 'Task C -> [A, B]' to visualize edges

verification.successMessage: Task and DAG data structures are correctly defined with dependency relationships!
verification.failureMessage: Print each task and its dependencies in the format 'Task <id> -> [dep1, dep2]'.

steps.title: Implement dependency graph
steps.description: Add `addTask(task)` and `addDependency(taskId, dependsOnId)` methods to the DAG class. `addDependency` should validate that both tasks exist and that adding the edge doesn't create a cycle (using DFS-based cycle detection). Build the sample DAG and print the adjacency list showing all edges between tasks.
hints: For cycle detection, run DFS from the task being added; if you encounter the dependency task, it's a cycle
Store adjacency list as a Map<string, string[]> from task ID to its dependents
Print the adjacency list as 'A -> [C, E]' meaning C and E depend on A

verification.successMessage: Dependency graph correctly validates edges and detects cycles!
verification.failureMessage: Print the adjacency list and also show that attempting a cycle returns an error message.

steps.title: Add topological sort
steps.description: Implement Kahn's algorithm to compute a topological ordering of the DAG. Compute in-degree for each task, start with zero in-degree tasks, process them, decrement in-degree of dependents, and repeat. Return the sorted execution order. Print the topological sort order for your DAG and verify it respects all dependencies.
hints: In-degree = number of direct dependencies a task has
When a task is processed, decrement in-degree of all its dependents; if any reach 0, add to queue
If the sorted result doesn't include all tasks, the graph has a cycle

verification.successMessage: Topological sort produces a valid execution order that respects all dependencies!
verification.failureMessage: Print the topological order: 'Execution order: A -> B -> C -> D -> E'.

steps.title: Implement parallel execution
steps.description: Extend the DAG to execute tasks in parallel where possible. Tasks with all dependencies resolved (in-degree 0) should run concurrently. Use the topological order to identify parallel batches: each batch contains independent tasks. Simulate execution with `setTimeout` or async/await (different durations per task). Print the execution timeline showing which tasks ran in parallel.
hints: Group tasks into waves: wave 0 = all tasks with in-degree 0, then process and collect next wave
Use Promise.all() to run each wave's tasks in parallel
Print 'Wave <N>: [taskA, taskB] running in parallel (duration: <X>ms)'

verification.successMessage: Parallel execution correctly identifies independent tasks and runs them concurrently!
verification.failureMessage: Print each execution wave showing which tasks run in parallel and their durations.

steps.title: Add error propagation and rollback
steps.description: Implement error handling: if a task fails, mark it as 'failed', propagate the failure to all dependent tasks (mark them as 'skipped'), and stop their execution. Build a rollback mechanism that runs a registered `rollback` function on each completed task when a dependent fails. Print the error chain showing which task failed and which were skipped.
hints: When a task fails, traverse its dependents recursively and mark them as 'skipped'
Run rollback on successfully completed tasks in reverse dependency order
Print 'Task <id> FAILED -> cascading: [taskC, taskD] SKIPPED, rolling back: [taskA]'

verification.successMessage: Error propagation correctly cascades failures to dependents and triggers rollback!
verification.failureMessage: Print the error chain: which task failed, which were skipped, and which were rolled back.

steps.title: Implement retry for failed tasks
steps.description: Add retry logic to task execution. Support `maxRetries` (configurable per task, default 3) and `retryDelayMs` (delay between retries). If a task fails and has remaining retries, wait and re-execute. Track retryAttempts on the task. Only propagate failure if all retries are exhausted. Print retry status showing attempt number for each retry.
hints: Wrap task execution in a retry loop: while attempts < maxRetries, try/catch with delay
Use setTimeout or sleep() between retry attempts
Print 'Task <id>: attempt 2/3 failed, retrying in <delay>ms...' and 'Task <id>: succeeded on attempt 2'

verification.successMessage: Retry logic correctly re-executes failed tasks and succeeds after configurable attempts!
verification.failureMessage: Print retry status showing 'Task <id>: attempt 2/3 - failed, retrying...' and final outcome.

steps.title: Build execution report
steps.description: Combine everything into a `runPipeline()` method that executes the DAG and returns a comprehensive report. The report should include for each task: id, status, duration (ms), attempts, startTime, endTime, result. Also include overall stats: totalDuration, totalTasks, completedCount, failedCount, skippedCount. Print the full execution report in a formatted table.
hints: Collect task execution data in a results Map as each task completes
Calculate totalDuration as max(endTime) - min(startTime) across all tasks
Print the report as a formatted table with columns: Task | Status | Duration | Attempts

verification.successMessage: Execution report provides complete task-level details and overall pipeline statistics!
verification.failureMessage: Print a formatted report showing each task's id, status, duration, attempts, and overall pipeline stats.
